That’s about 5,000 more than even the Ministry of Justice accepts can be held safely on the prison estate. But that’s not a new story – prisons have been full for years now. They were full when David Cameron was prime minister. They were full under Boris Johnson – and Liz Truss and Rishi Sunak. And when Keir Starmer became prime minister, he inherited a system about to collapse – unless he carried on with Conservative plans to release some prisoners early.     New Carrier To Replace USS Lincoln in Middle East | Balance of Power: Late Edition 08/13/2026
    "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Former Secretary of Defense Mark Esper, says he agrees with President Trump's strategy for an economic blockade and expects US forces to remain in the region for an extended period. Cait Conley, Democratic Candidate for US House in New York's 17th District, says data centers can be a net positive for communities. Sen. Jack Reed (D-RI) says the Pentagon has failed to adequately communicate with both Republicans and Democrats about operations in Iran. (Source: Bloomberg)
    Money Flow Linked to Human Smuggling Plunges in Trump Crackdown
    Reports of possible transactions for human smuggling through money-transfer businesses and banks fell by over 60% in 2025, according to a US Treasury report.
    Esper: Expect US To Be in Region for Extended Time
    Former Secretary of Defense Mark Esper, says he agrees with President Trump's strategy for an economic blockade and expects US forces to remain in the region for an extended period. Esper says the US failed to reinvigorate its defense industrial base quickly enough to build the stockpiles and production capacity needed for a major conflict. Esper says that responsibility for conditions on the USS Lincoln fall on the leadership onboard the ship and that the length of deployment is what falls on the Secretary of Defense. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
    Conley: AI Can Be Net Positive for Communities
    Cait Conley, Democratic Candidate for US House in New York's 17th District, says data centers can be a net positive for communities. Conley notes AI poses serious risks and that companies need to do the right thing as the technology advances. Conley also discusses her race against Rep. Mike Lawler (R-NY) and the controversy surrounding Rep. Max Miller's (R-OH) donation to Lawler's race. She speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
    Reed: No Good Choices at Moment With Iran
    Sen. Jack Reed (D-RI) says the Pentagon has failed to adequately communicate with both Republicans and Democrats about operations in Iran. Reed says that issues with prolonged deployments and operations are not isolated to USS Abraham Lincoln but as well as other ships and units on the ground. Reed says Senate Armed Services Committee Chairman Roger Wicker shares concerns about the Lincoln and that the issue should come before the committee. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
    Trump Agreed to Consider Australia Tariff Request, Albanese Says
    US President Donald Trump has agreed to Australia’s request to “consider full exemption or, at the very least, no increase” to the tariffs imposed by the US, Australia’s Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Friday.

    Bloomberg Intelligence Chief US Interest Rate Strategist Ira Jersey talks 30-year bonds hitting highest interest rates since 2001. From erratic rains in India to intense heat in Europe, weather extremes are threatening crops, supply chains, energy sources — and human life. Tell people you’re testing air conditioning, and the truth soon comes out: far more people have aircon than you’d ever imagine. It’s a guilty secret, the home improvement equivalent of Botox or weight loss jabs – everyone notices the results, but nobody admits to the method. Most portable aircons are in bedrooms, hidden away from visitors, so they’re easy to keep secret. And while friends with aircon don’t suddenly look younger or slimmer, they do look suspiciously well rested during a heatwave, while you’ve spent the night tossing and turning. So if you’re using an aircon unit, why have it in the bedroom? Warm air rises, so upstairs bedrooms can be the hottest by the end of the day, making for restless nights.
